question: Can a continual topic model that carries a prior forward across time slices beat a sequential online LDA baseline on topic coherence and topic stability over a text stream?
method: Stratified 80/20 split of 20 Newsgroups; training part cut into 5 random time slices; sequential online LDA (20 topics) vs the same LDA where, after each slice, the topic-word matrix is blended with the pre-slice matrix (weight chosen by cross-validation on an inner split of the training data over {0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75}); evaluated by NPMI on held-out test docs, stability and LR macro-F1; 3 seeds.
metric_name: NPMI topic coherence of top-10 words on held-out test documents
baseline: Standard sequential online LDA (sklearn LatentDirichletAllocation, partial_fit per slice, 20 topics); stand-in, not the paper's neural CoNTM.
improved: Same online LDA and same slices, but after each partial_fit the topic-word matrix is blended with the pre-slice matrix as a continual prior; blend weight selected by CV on training data only. No extra fits or data.
notes: Topic stability compares index-aligned topics across consecutive slices. The improved model performs no extra LDA fits; its only additional cost is the blend step and a small inner CV over 4 blend weights on training data (seed 42 only), which is run before the test evaluation. The baseline (mix=0 equivalent) is part of the grid, so the selected setting is never worse than the baseline on the validation split. The 20 Newsgroups data has no timestamps, so random slices simulate a stream. Results are from a small seed count and a single data split.
